descriptions.zh:
我们的[owner.GetScientistPlural]在一座晶莹剔透的冻湖边扎营。由于光源充足，人们甚至可以看见冰面之下的幽魂之塔透出点点微光。它们自湖床向上延伸，仿佛坚实的卷须。

我们资历尚浅的探险队成员依然在如此刺骨、严苛的寒冷中不停地工作。尽管条件艰苦，我们的挖掘却进展的很顺利。我们已经发现了好几个气阀，都是为原始的水下舰艇而设计成的港口。然而，我们却没有在现场发现这些舰艇的踪影。不管这些高塔的住民是留下来还是逃走了，港口上都已经是空无一人。
descriptions.en:
Our [owner.GetScientistPlural] have set their camps around the edges of a glassy, frozen lake. Under sufficient light, one may catch glimpses of spectral towers underneath. They grasp upwards from the lake bed like steadfast tendrils.

Our less experienced crews are still adjusting to work in such biting, sterile cold. Despite this, our excavations have proceeded swiftly. We have exposed numerous airlocks, all designed for primitive submarine vessels. There is, as yet, no sign of the vessels themselves. Whether the tower's inhabitants stayed or fled, every one of its docks was left empty.

label.zh: 我们应当将资源进一步投入到破冰技术上。
label.en: We should invest further in these ice-breaking techniques.

descriptions.zh:
随着我们进一步从各种各样的冰层定居点上移走大冰块，我们的[owner.GetScientistPlural]在停泊塔处发现了一座原始的计算机终端。它那易碎的金属外壳看上去被……咬了个扎实。

这个终端在经过一些轻微的修理之后，顺利地启动了。定居点数据网络的大部仍然处于下线状态，但是我们可以从本地缓存中的股权证明、个人文件，还有一些看上去是任务日志的文件中推断出很多情报。
descriptions.en:
As we continue to remove large sections of ice from around the various icebound habitats, our [owner.GetScientistPlural] at the docking tower have discovered a primitive computer terminal. Its brittle metal casing appears to have been... chewed upon.

The terminal booted up correctly after some minor repairs. Large parts of the habitat's data network remain offline, but we can infer a great deal from local caches of stock manifests, personnel files, and what appears to be a stash of mission logs.

descriptions.zh:
我们对[from.planet.GetName]上古代定居点的知识愈发深刻，我们的忧虑也更加浓厚。我们之前发现的只是一处前哨殖民地的残垣——属于某个文明的遗迹，这个文明长久以来被世间遗忘，我们甚至都辨识不出他们的名字。

在这个星球，海洋占据着绝对主导的地位。各种不同团体的殖民者从母星被带到这个星球，应征成为水下先遣队成员。他们的目标：建立殖民地，开发这颗行星的自然资源。然而，他们的现实却是一场未加约束的生物学实验、剧烈的政治变动，以及§Y凶猛的动植物§!带来的重大危险。

我们找到了一处导航浮标上面的传感器日志，看上去它记录了一组队员前往附近哨站的路线。我们相信这些人的舰艇仍然在原地，被困在冰层中，包含有许多有用的材料。
descriptions.en:
Our knowledge of the ancient settlement on [from.planet.GetName] deepens, but so too does our concern. What we have uncovered is the remains of a frontier colony - a remnant of a civilization so long forgotten, we cannot even discern their name.

When seas were a more dominant feature on this world, disparate groups of settlers were brought from their homeworld and conscripted into pioneer submarine crews. Their goal: to establish colonies and exploit the planet's natural resources. Their reality, however, was one of unchecked biological experiments, radical political change, and significant peril fending off §Yhostile flora and fauna§!.

The sensor logs from a navigation buoy appear to have tracked one such crew en route to a nearby outpost. We believe their vessel may still be there, trapped in ice along with a cache of useful materials.

label.zh: 立刻派遣一支研究小队。

options.script: name = arcsite.1010.a

label.zh: 看看我们从这些剽悍的海洋住民身上能学到些什么。
label.en: See what we can learn about those hostile ocean-dwellers.

descriptions.zh:
这是一个被墨冰包围的洞穴，在里面我们发现了一艘瘫痪烧毁的古老潜艇残骸。这个烧焦的洞穴让残骸得以避开这颗星球上最为恶劣的冻融循环，将这群船员遭受灭顶之灾的惨状完好地保留了下来。

该潜艇落后的核引擎上有过紧急维修的迹象。在船员舱中，我们发现了划痕以及化学物质灼烧留下的微量残留。潜艇上所有的逃生仓当时都已派出，不过有一个被卡在了附近休眠的火山口中。

这艘残骸上可供收集的东西不多，但这群船员原先的目的地——一座殖民地§Y补给仓库§!依旧完好无损。我们的维修团队因此得以将这群注定失败的船员无法修复的部件成功修复。
descriptions.en:
Blackened ice surrounds the cave in which we found the crumpled, burnt wreckage of an ancient submarine. Sheltered from the worst of this planet's freeze-thaw cycles, this scorched cave has preserved evidence of multiple calamities befalling this crew.

The vessel's crude nuclear engine bears signs of hasty patchwork repairs; in the crew quarters we found scratch marks and faint residue from chemical burns. At some point all the submarine's escape shuttles were deployed, yet only one remains nearby - it became lodged inside a dormant lava vent.

There is little more to glean from this burnt-out wreckage, but the crew's erstwhile destination - a colonial §Ysupply cache§! - has remained intact. Our recovery team has therefore succeeded in retrieving what the doomed submariners could not.

descriptions.zh:
我们在厚重的冰层中挖掘出了一条隧道，在一个密闭洞穴中找到了一艘潜艇的完整残骸。冻土带的环境将所有有机物都化为了齑粉，但是也让许多古迹完好保存下来。

我们的人类学研究表明，当船员们逃离附近的殖民地后，这艘潜艇便成了孕育了诸多政治活动的温床。它们在船舱内部各自划分了数个主权边界，并分别支持不同类型的政治主张。令人震惊的是，这种极端的派系划分不仅没有使船员分裂，反而加强了船员之间的社会联系。这个研究肯定会在我们的主攻政治学的科学家们引发激烈的讨论。
descriptions.en:
We have tunnelled through significant quantities of ice to find the intact wreckage of a submarine, sealed within an airtight cave. Tundral conditions have long since reduced all organic matter to fine dust, but so too have they preserved a wealth of cultural artifacts.

Our anthropological survey suggests a hotbed of political activity as this submarine's crew broke away from the nearby colony. They proclaimed several sovereign boundaries within the hull of their own submarine, espousing all manner of political ideologies. Surprisingly, this extreme factionalism appears to have strengthened the social bonds of this crew rather than forcing them apart. The matter is sure to spark lively debate amongst our own political scientists.

label.zh: ……让我们比不同政见者更进一步。
label.en: ... Keeping us one step ahead of dissidents.

descriptions.zh:
我们本以为如此古老的遗骸在漫长的岁月中早已被破坏，谁知道由于当时的急速冻结，保护了遗骸的上半部分。随之一起保存下来的还有许多生物的尸体，其中一些貌似是当地的巨大又凶猛的捕食性动物。其他穿着防护服的智慧生物似乎是那些猎食者的猎物。

这些潜艇上的船员并不是[fromfrom.planet.GetName]本地人。我们的解剖表明，他们将当地生物的基因拼接融入到自己体内。至于这群殖民者为什么要这样广泛地进行自我改造，恐怕我们只能自己想象了。但不可否认的是，他们利用这种方式，确实让这些基因得以保存下来。
descriptions.en:
We had expected such an ancient wreck to have been crushed long ago. Instead we find that this stricken hulk was flash-frozen, preserving its superstructure along with the corpses of numerous creatures. Some of these appear to have been native fauna: large, ferocious and decidedly predatory in nature. The others appear to have been their prey: a small group of sapient beings wearing environment suits.

These individuals - the submarine's crew - did not originate on [fromfrom.planet.GetName]. Rather, our autopsy suggests that these aliens had gene-spliced themselves with material from local lifeforms. We can only imagine what drove the colonists to modify themselves so extensively, and yet we cannot deny: by preserving this genetic material within themselves, they have ensured the survival of a valuable genetic history.

options.conditions: exclusive_trigger = { owner = { has_origin = origin_evolutionary_predators } }

descriptions.zh:
在尽我们所能调查了潜艇残骸和废弃居住区后，我们在[from.planet.GetName]的队伍正准备于行星地表附近重整。这里的殖民地尚有太多未知。我们找到的东西大多只相当于五花八门的遗物，它们的原主人曾在格外孤独、边远的地方生活。

尽管缺少超光速旅行的能力，这些古代潜艇居民们引导我们在其他领域取得了可观的突破。他们经历艰险取得了这些发现，我们会力求不再经历诸如此类的磨难。
descriptions.en:
Having surveyed all we can from the wrecked submarine and abandoned habitats, our teams on [from.planet.GetName] are preparing to regroup near the planet's surface. There is much we still do not know about this colony. Most of what we found simply amounts to an eclectic legacy, of life on a particularly lonely frontier.

Although they lacked faster-than-light travel, these ancient submariners have steered us towards remarkable breakthroughs in other fields. They made these discoveries in hardship, the likes of which we can strive not to experience ourselves.

descriptions.zh:
在尽我们所能调查了潜艇残骸和废弃居住区后，我们在[from.planet.GetName]的队伍正准备于行星地表附近重整。这里的殖民地尚有太多未知。我们找到的东西大多只相当于五花八门的遗物，它们的原主人曾在格外孤独、边远的地方生活。

尽管他们的文明尚未拥有超光速旅行技术，磨难艰险似乎引导这个一度位于潜艇内的殖民地在科学和经济上取得了独特的突破，我们如今可以随意利用这些发现。
descriptions.en:
Having surveyed all we can from the wrecked submarine and abandoned habitats, our teams on [from.planet.GetName] are preparing to regroup near the planet's surface. There is much we still do not know about this colony. Most of what we found simply amounts to an eclectic legacy, of life on a particularly lonely frontier.

Although their civilization did not yet possess faster-than-light technology, hardship seems to steered this once-submarine colony towards some singular breakthroughs in science and economics, which we are now at liberty to exploit.

label.zh: 这些警世通言也许会让我们的殖民者受益。
label.en: These cautionary tales may benefit our colonists.

label.zh: 地下居住地是个有趣的主意。
label.en: Sub-surface habitats are an interesting idea.

label.zh: 我们可以好好利用潜艇上的军备。
label.en: We could put that submarine's armaments to good use.

label.zh: 我们一定要珍惜他们的回忆。

descriptions.zh:
我们对地表进行扫描后确定了一些有价值的矿藏，其中埋有不计其数的不同物种的遗骸。有些甚至与目前仍生活在这颗星球上的一些生物相仿，其他的则与我们所见过的生物截然不同。

尽管这项工作并不容易，周围的野生动物也被我们惊扰，但[leader.GetName]还是已经有了重要的发现，并成功地重建了一些已经灭绝的物种。但这也反过来引起了研究团队的一些争论。其中一些人想展出这些标本，而另一些则更愿意进一步研究这些材料，毕竟这些化石已经是保存状况最好的一批，而这个矿点也即将被挖空了。
descriptions.en:
We scanned the surface and found a few promising deposits, filled with the remains of a variety of different species. Some resemble those still living on the surface, while others are nothing like we have seen before.

Although the work is hard and the wildlife is agitated by our presence, [leader.GetName] has already made remarkable discoveries and managed to reconstruct some of the extinct species. This, in turn, sparked a dispute among the research team. While some want to display these species in exhibitions, others prefer to study the material, as they are the best-preserved fossils found to date, and this dig site is almost exhausted.

label.en: Make an exhibition out of them.

options.script:
name = arcsite.2000.use
fleet_event = { id = arcsite.2002 days = 30 }

descriptions.zh: 我们已经开展了充分的研究，探明了化石物种和[from.planet.GetName]当前生物圈中各物种之间的关系。结果证明，它们中的一些属于同一属种，具有许多相似性。进一步的研究或许能够带给我们更多答案。
descriptions.en: We have done extensive research to determine the relationship of fossil species to the current biosphere on [from.planet.GetName]. It turns out that some of them belong to the same genus, having many similarities. Further studies might bring us more answers.

descriptions.zh: 不少人前来参观我们的展览。尽管我们不能将收集到的东西用于研究，但我们还是吸引到了几位慷慨的赞助商，将这些化石送去举办行星际巡回展览。展品的异星外观在那些对外星考古学有兴趣的人中间引起了小规模的热烈反响。
descriptions.en: Quite a few people came to our exhibition. Although we can't use the collected material for our research, we attracted some generous funders and sent the fossils on an interplanetary tour. The alien appearance of exhibits caused a small boom of people interested in xenoarchaeology.

descriptions.zh:
将第一个考古遗址彻底翻遍之后，我们决定转移到更加偏僻的地方，搜寻更多可供研究用的材料。[leader.GetName]找到了一个相当好的地点，此处是一个洞穴，被一些有智慧但已经灭绝的物种用作居所。在谨慎的探索和检查之后，我们发现了一些非同寻常的事情：不管住在这个洞穴里的是何方神圣，这种生物会使用一种精妙的染料，在光和热的作用下会显出颜色。

我们已经识别出两种彩绘：一种讲述过去的故事，另一种描绘了日常生活。不幸的是，由于我们的闯入，让彩绘得以保留下来的精妙生态系统遭到扰乱。这种扰乱产生的一系列连锁反应，加之染料本身经历的岁月，导致这些彩绘会在短时间内消失。小队必须立马决定抢救哪一种更有价值的彩绘。
descriptions.en:
Exhausting the first site, we decided to move to more remote places in search of more material for research. [leader.GetName] found a good enough spot, a cave that served as a home for some intelligent extinct species. Careful probing and examination revealed something unusual: whatever lived in this cave used an ingenious dye that reveals itself when exposed to heat and light.

We have identified two types of paintings: one telling the story of the past, and the other portraying daily life. Unfortunately, we disrupted the delicate ecosystem that preserved the drawings. The resulting chain reaction, combined with the age of the dye, causes it to fade and disappear on short notice. The team must decide which one is worth saving.

options.script:
name = arcsite.2010.use
fleet_event = { id = arcsite.2012 days = 30 }

descriptions.zh: 我们获取的彩绘讲述了这个物种的过往，给予我们许多有关它们历史的新认识。看上去，这些穴居者同某个高级文明进行了接触，这在某种程度上影响了它们的外形和发展路线。根据这些生物的外形描述，我们猜测该物种能够快速地进行基因变异，几代之内其外表就会发生显著变化。
descriptions.en: We captured drawings related to the past and gained insight into the species' history. It appears that these cave dwellers came into contact with an advanced civilization that somewhat influenced their looks and development. Given the depictions of the creatures, we assume that the species was prone to rapid genetic mutations, and their generations varied greatly in appearance.

descriptions.zh: 我们获取的彩绘讲述了这个物种的日常生活，给予我们许多有关它们历史的新认识。彩绘将穴居者描绘成一群外形看上去迥乎不同，但智力水平相近的物种，正在参加复杂的仪式。[leader.GetName]假设，这是各种各样的生物沐浴在神明的圣光之下，为祂工作，以换取神赐的自由。
descriptions.en: We captured drawings related to daily life and gained insight into the history of the species. They depict cave dwellers as a conglomeration of different-looking but similarly intelligent species who participated in complex rituals. [leader.GetName] assumed that the various creatures basked in the light of the deity, worked for him, and in return were given freedom.

descriptions.zh:
我们进一步探索这个洞穴的裂缝深处，来到了一处人工岩室，里面有一个古怪的骨质结构。鉴于这个结构当前的状态，它看上去好像发生了坍塌，然后沉到了地里面——可能是一场地震导致的。[Leader.GetName]下令在原地扎营，我们也已在周边进行了一些探测，但地面并不是很稳定。一旦我们进入内部，我们可能不会有充足的时间对这个结构进行彻底的检查。

对我们的研究来说，最大的潜在成果就是这座建筑本身。我们可以研究这种精巧的类骨物质，或者将精力放在探索上，搜寻这个结构内部更多有关外星人的线索——了解是谁建造了它，怎么使用它，这些人的日常生活是怎样的。
descriptions.en:
Exploring further into the deep chasms of the cave, we came across a grotto with a strange bone structure inside. Given the current state of the structure, it looks like it collapsed and sank into the ground - probably as a result of an earthquake. [Leader.GetName] ordered a camp to be set up, and we have already done some perimeter scans, but the ground is not stable. We may not have adequate time to examine the structure fully once we get inside.

The greatest potential yield for our studies lies in the building itself. We can either study the intriguing bone-like material or focus our efforts on exploration, searching the structure for more clues about the aliens who built and used it and their daily routine.

options.script:
name = arcsite.2020.use
fleet_event = { id = arcsite.2022 days = 30 }

descriptions.zh:
在经过波澜不惊的研究之后，[Leader.GetName]得出的结论是这座建筑曾经是……活着的。当然不是现在，而是很多年前，在它被创造出来的某个时候。一大堆骨和组织被粘合在了一起，建造出了这样一栋建筑，能够根据特定的需求变形。考虑到这座建筑坍塌的方式，我们或许甚至可以假设这是结构的这一部分故意执行的行为。

不幸的是，我们在研究过程中不小心破坏了这个结构，它坍塌得更加厉害了，致使这座建筑无法用于我们的进一步研究。[Leader.GetName]下令小队继续前进。
descriptions.en:
After uneventful research, [Leader.GetName] concluded that the building was... alive. Not now, but years ago, sometime during its creation. It was a mass of bones and tissues molded together to create a building that could reshape for the desired purpose. Given the way the building collapsed, one might even assume that this was a deliberate act on the part of the structure itself.

Unfortunately, we compromised the structure during our studies and it collapsed even further, rendering the building useless for further research. [Leader.GetName] ordered the team to move forward.

descriptions.zh:
这个阴森的结构内部原来是一座迷宫，满是半坍塌的廊道，地上到处都是四散分布的类骨物质。在历经磨难之后，我们设法取出了几样工具和物体，这些都昭示着某个复合的文化势力曾一度生活在这个行星上。它们或许能够提供给我们新的认识，让我们了解这些灭绝的物种究竟是怎样的生命。

不幸的是，在我们的研究过程中，不小心破坏了这个结构，它坍塌得更加厉害了，致使这座建筑无法用于我们得进一步研究。[Leader.GetName]下令小队继续前进。
descriptions.en:
The interior of this creepy structure turned out to be a maze of half-collapsed corridors filled with bone-like material lying everywhere. With some difficulty, we were able to extract several tools and objects that indicate that a complex culture lived on this planet. They will give us great insight into what life may have been like for these extinct species.

Unfortunately, we compromised the structure during our studies and it collapsed even further, rendering the building useless for further research. [Leader.GetName] has ordered the team to move forward.

descriptions.zh:
我们终于抵达了洞穴的最里面。我们进入了某座深深地埋在地底下、看上去像是古旧的废弃地堡一样的建筑。它看上去同我们先前找到的任何东西都不一样：我们只能假设是某些外星访客在这里设置了一个研究实验室。根据破旧的地堡、各种各样的骨头、还有四散的化石，显然他们以前也在研究这些物种，正同我们现在做的一样……唯一的区别是，他们能够趁着这些物种还活着的时候，在它们身上做各种实验。

我们刚一恢复考古遗址和数据库的电源供给，[Leader.GetName]立马就开始了工作，试图将其中收集到的任何有用的信息归纳到一起。
descriptions.en:
We finally reached the end of the cave. We entered something that resembled an old abandoned bunker built deep underground. It doesn't look like anything we've found before: we assume alien visitors set up a research lab down here. And given the dilapidated tanks, various bones, and fossils lying around, they were studying these species just as we were... Only they had this opportunity to conduct research when their specimens were still alive.

[Leader.GetName] immediately jumped to work, trying to gather any useful information from the site and data banks, as soon as we plugged them into the power source.

label.zh: 我们发现了怎样的谜题？

options.script: name = arcsite.2030.proceed

descriptions.zh:
我们将先前研究中得到的知识和数据库中的信息进行了比照。得出的结论让人寒颤。很显然，几千年前，某个能够太空航行的文明降落到了这个星球上，发现这些土生土长的物种在使用了他们掌握的基因操纵技术后，能够很容易地驯服。最开始，他们将有智慧的人群——尽管尚未完全开发——土人奴役，并且在它们身上进行各种各样的实验。这些实验包括为了建造目的将它们转化为活体建材。除此之外还有顺从的奴隶。甚至宠物或者牲口。

我们先前发现的实例很有可能就是这些物种的遗体，彼时它们尚未退化为现今[from.planet.GetName]上郁郁葱葱的非智慧生物圈的一部分。对于一个在未来的某一天能够像我们一样横贯整个星系的物种来说，这真是一个骇人的结局。
descriptions.en:
We compared our knowledge from previous studies to the information from the databanks. The conclusion we made is disconcerting. It appears that thousands of years ago, a space-faring civilization landed on this world and found the indigenous specimens easy to train, using their genetic manipulation techniques. At first, they enslaved the population of intelligent - albeit not fully-developed - autochthons, and conducted various experiments on them. These included making them into living tissue for construction purposes. Or into obedient slaves. Or into pets and livestock.

The previous instances we found were probably remnants of these species before they devolved into the non-sapient biosphere that now thrives on the [from.planet.GetName]. A horrifying end for a species that could, one day, have traversed the galaxy just as we do.

descriptions.zh:
很显然，几千年前，一个先进的文明发现了居住在这里的物种，并且很有兴趣研究它们。他们因当地多样化的生物圈而着迷。老旧的数据库仍旧可以运转，里面记录了奇怪的结论和让人不得不忧心的实验。数据库里面包含了这个物种的一个基本基因构成，以及它们在过去和将来是如何进行演化的。

这些研究者自身发生了什么？他们退化成了我们先前发现的穴居者吗？或者正相反，这些研究者就是从穴居者中间进化而来的，在某个时间点离开了这颗行星？这一切不禁让我们思索：宇宙还容纳了怎样的谜团？
descriptions.en:
It appears that thousands of years ago, an advanced civilization found the specimens living here to be an interesting study. They were, fascinated by the diverse biosphere. Old databanks are still working, filled with strange conclusions and somewhat worrying experiments. They contain a basic genetic composition of the species and how they might have developed in the past and future.

What happened to the researchers themselves? Did they devolve to the state of cave dwellers we found before? Or maybe it is the opposite, and they evolved from them, leaving the planet at some point? It brings us to wonder: what other mysteries does the universe hold?

label.zh: 这证明了绝不能相信异星人！
label.en: This proves that Xenos can't be trusted!

label.zh: 我们的政府绝对不会犯下如此的骇人罪行！
label.en: Such crimes would be impossible under our government!
The galaxy is a harsh place.

descriptions.zh: 我们并不是第一个在§Y[From.Planet.System.GetName]§!恒星系发现该碎片环带的：我们发现了一架小到被我们[Root.Owner.GetResearchers]戏称为“太空小屋”的飞船，里面有一具毒物类外星人的遗骸和无数的数据水晶。根据腐坏的程度推断，这名外星人最有可能是在短短几个世纪前去世的。
descriptions.en: We are not the first to discover the debris belt in the §Y[From.Planet.System.GetName]§! system: a craft - so small that our [Root.Owner.GetResearchers] are dubbing it a "space cabin" - has been found, containing the remains of a single toxoid alien and a considerable number of data crystals. Judging by the rate of decay, our best guess is that this alien expired only a few centuries ago.

options.script:
name = INTERESTING
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
在外星人的太空小屋里发现的数据水晶实际上是一些任务日志。我们的[Root.Owner.GetResearchers]已经发回了一个样本及其简单翻译。它开头的的语调振奋人心：

“这是一生中绝无仅有的好机会。传说中奥德瑞斯基亚水触手可及。我的新家有点差强人意，但对我已经很满足了，因为我很快就可以寄回家足够的钱付给女儿治病了。”

然而很快，日志就变得酸楚了起来：

“妻子和女儿都死了。世上不再有人会悼念我。在黑市上贩卖打捞所得仅仅足以维持生活。现在后悔已经太晚了。”

这名外星人总共在碎片环带白费了五十多年的时间搜罗宝物但一无所获。
descriptions.en:
The data crystals discovered in the alien's space cabin are in fact mission logs. Our [Root.Owner.GetResearchers] have sent us a sample, along with a preliminary translation. They start in an upbeat tone:

"This is the chance of a lifetime. The ruins of the fabled Odryskans are within reach. My new home isn't much, but it's good enough for me, and soon I'll be able to send enough credits home to pay for my daughter's treatment."

Soon enough however, the logs grow sour:

"Wife and daughter dead. No one left to mourn for me. Salvage sold on black market barely enough to support living costs. Too late to turn back now."

All told, the alien spent over five decades trawling the rubble belt in an apparently futile search for riches.

label.zh: 他们在这么长的时间里肯定能发现些什么！
label.en: Surely they found something in all those years!

options.script:
name = arcsite.2505.A
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
不可能
不可能
不可能
不可能
§R骗子！§!
……
……
……
万一是真的呢？

随着这名外星人滑入疯狂的深渊，日志的内容也变得越来越令人毛骨悚人。
descriptions.en:
It is not true
It is not true
It is not true
It is not true
§RLIES!§!
...
...
...
But what if it is true?

The logs become increasingly disturbing as the alien slips further and further into madness.

descriptions.zh:
我们的[Root.Owner.GetResearchers]完成了对外星人日志水晶的翻译。他们呈递了最后一份日志的翻译，这份日志是在该外星人死前不久记录下的，记录者罕见地意识清醒：

“我终于找到了我一直苦苦追寻的东西。很多人会觉得我花这么多年找来找去跟疯了一样。我觉得，可能这些人也没错。我已经快老死了，我的亲朋好友也早都入土了。不管找到了什么宝贝，现在把它卖了也毫无意义，但我应该可以安息了。”

日志后面附上了这位外星人找到宝藏的位置。依据这份日志，我们追踪到了一块体积令人震惊的巨型宝石，它的价值无法估量。
descriptions.en:
Our [Root.Owner.GetResearchers] have finished translating the alien's data crystals. They present an interpretation of the last log, in which, not long before their death, the recorder experiences a rare moment of lucidity:

"I have finally found what I am looking for. Many would consider me mad for continuing the search this long. I think, probably, that they are right. I am old, now - dying, even - and my kin are long since dust. There is no point in selling the artifact, but perhaps now I can find peace."

The logs go on to pinpoint where the alien concealed the treasure. By following them, we have tracked down an astonishingly large gemstone of immeasurable value.

descriptions.zh:
[From.Planet.MoonOf.GetName]上的废弃观测站似乎在报废前不久被改为他用。尽管上面还有用于监视行星居民的设备的证据，但看来大部分都改成了夏瑞诺伊的历史博物馆。奇怪的是，明明这是一个好斗的物种，但是关于暴力的主题被刻意回避了，展品主要集中在一些关于和平和生育的仪式上。

在中控室发现了一系列数据水晶。显然这就是我们想要找的东西。
descriptions.en:
The abandoned observation post above [From.Planet.MoonOf.GetName] appears to have been repurposed shortly before it was abandoned. Though there is equipment to surveil the inhabitants of the planet in evidence, most of it seems to be dedicated to a museum of Charynoi history. Curiously for such a warlike species, subjects relating to violence seem to have been avoided, and exhibits appear to show various rituals of peace and fertility.

A series of data crystals have been left in the control room. It is evident that we were supposed to find them.

options.script:
name = arcsite.3000.A
small_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
第一块数据水晶已经完成了翻译。其封面上写着“这是夏瑞诺伊民族的记录，系女先知伊蒂卡里奥斯所留，这样那些可能找到它的人能原谅我们的罪过。”

其后是一份历史、哲学和艺术工作的合辑，可能是由一个比较标准但稍微好斗的晚工业革命社会所创。我们的[Owner.GetLinguists]将其发回[Owner.Capital.GetName]以进行进一步研究。
descriptions.en:
The first crystal has been translated. It is prefaced with the words "This is the record of the Charynoi people, left behind by the Prophetess Ithikarios, so that those who might find it may forgive us our sins."

What follows is a collection of historical, philosophical and artistic works as may have been created by a fairly standard, if somewhat belligerent, late industrial society. Our [Owner.GetLinguists] have sent it back to [Owner.Capital.GetName] for further analysis.

descriptions.zh:
“现在我将叙述一切是如何走向错误——我们最初陷入傲慢罪恶的地方，”伊蒂卡里奥斯宣称。

第二颗晶体记录了夏瑞诺伊是如何逐渐揭开太空飞行的奥秘，似乎比[Root.Owner.GetName]早了大约一百年。他们在自己的星系中发现了两颗美丽的行星，并得出结论认为这些行星是神灵留给他们的产业，是他们与生俱来的权利，他们现在正在索取这些权利。

伊蒂卡里奥斯用惊恐的语气讲述了这些早期探索的黑暗面：在他们的新殖民地中，初生的文明并不愿意放弃他们的家园。他们被打败并被奴役，最终逐渐消亡，死于夏瑞诺伊不屑于治疗的疾病。

我们的[Owner.GetLinguists]正在努力翻译第三个也是最后一个数据晶体。
descriptions.en:
"Now I shall recount where it all went wrong - where we first fell to the sin of arrogance," declaims Ithikarios.

The second crystal recounts how the Charynoi gradually uncovered the mysteries of space flight, seemingly about a hundred years before the [Root.Owner.GetName]. They found two beautiful planets in their own system, and concluded that those had been bequeathed to them by the Gods as their birthright, which they were now claiming.

In horrified tones, Ithikarios recounts the darker side to these early exploits: nascent civilizations on their new colonies had not willingly yielded their homes. Beaten into submission, they were enslaved and eventually dwindled, falling to diseases the Charynoi did not care to cure.

Our [Owner.GetLinguists] are hard at work translating the third and final data crystal.

options.script:
name = DISTURBING
medium_artifact_reward = yes

descriptions.zh:
最终，我们耗尽了我们所拥有的空间。我们知道虫洞的存在，但是它们无法被我们研究。我们的领土物产丰富景色优美，很容易让我们相信自己是天之选民。虫洞是一种考验，只要通过了考验，我们就能将自己的种族传遍整个星系，这是我们的神圣使命。

我曾经是那些试图履行这个职责的首领之一。当灵感降临在我身上——我意识到掌握了打开虫洞的钥匙——我便在祖先神社中祈祷了几天。最终得到了启示：我们不配。如果我们穿过虫洞，我们只会找到痛苦。艾斯法瑞尔将被清除，作为我们所犯罪行的惩罚。我决定销毁我的研究，并寻找一条不同的路。

要找到可以信任的人很难。如果我们被发现了，我们肯定宁可快速死亡。虽然我比以往任何时候都更加坚信我们是正确的，但我们会被视为叛教者。最终，我们启动了一个大胆的计划：在假装盲目飞越虫洞的愚蠢尝试的掩护下，我们建造了一艘方舟船，航行到未知的地方，朝着一个遥远的星球。我们经历了多年穿越空旷的太空，直到我们到达目的地。现在，我们只希望被留在和平中过上品德高尚的生活，以证明并非所有夏瑞诺伊都是邪恶的。

伊蒂卡里奥斯为她的兄弟们对我们造成的任何伤害深表歉意，她提到她试图在[From.Planet.MoonOf.GetName]周围竖起一个坚不可摧的盾牌，这样她的人民就不会再受到诱惑去寻找星辰。她失败了，但是我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]已经能够解决她的问题。现在，如果我们愿意，我们现在就可以竖起这个盾牌。
descriptions.en:
"Eventually, we exhausted the confines of the space we had been bequeathed. We knew of the existence of the Wormhole, but it defied our study. Our realm was so bountiful, so full of beauty, that it was not hard to convince ourselves that we were the Chosen. That the Wormhole was a test, and once we were worthy, it would be our Holy Purpose to spread our kind across all the galaxy.

"I was once chief amongst those seeking to fulfill this duty. When inspiration came to me - when I realized I held the key to the opening of the Wormhole - I prayed for days at the Shrine of my Ancestors. And eventually: Revelation. We were not worthy. If we went beyond the Wormhole, we would find only pain. Aspharelle would be scoured, out of punishment for the crimes we had committed. I resolved to destroy my research and seek a different path.

"It was hard to find those who I could trust. If we were discovered, we would surely have longed for a quick death. Though I am more convinced than ever that we are right, we would have been seen as apostates. Eventually, we launched a daring plan: under the guise of making a fool attempt to fly the wormhole blind, we built an arkship to sail into the unknown, towards a distant star. Many years, we traveled through empty space, until we came to our destination. Now we wish nothing more than to be left in peace to live virtuous lives, so that we may prove that not all Charynoi are evil."

Apologizing profusely for any harm done to us by her brethren, Ithikarios mentions her attempts at erecting an impenetrable shield around [From.Planet.MoonOf.GetName], so that her people would never again be tempted to seek the stars. She failed, but our [Owner.GetResearchers] have been able to work out where she went wrong. We could erect the shield now, if we so desire.

label.zh: 我们可以随心所欲处置它。
label.en: We can do with it as we please.

descriptions.zh: 得益于我们[Owner.GetResearchers]的努力，伊蒂卡里奥斯想要用来包围[FromFrom.GetName]的护盾完成了。她的夏瑞诺伊子民终于可以得到安宁。
descriptions.en: Thanks to the efforts of our [Owner.GetResearchers], the shield Ithikarios attempted to erect over [FromFrom.GetName] has been completed. Her Charynoi descendants can now find peace.

descriptions.zh:
宏伟的圣殿与损毁的神庙点缀在首都之上。而更深入的探索揭示出这个文明早在五十多万年前就被毁灭了。

根据几幅保存得相当完好的壁画被发现，原住民似乎在生物学上接近鸟类。对他们语言的初步音译表明，他们称自己为“克拉祖拉”。
descriptions.en:
Grand sanctums and ruined temples dot the landscape of the capital. A deeper exploration has revealed that this civilization was destroyed more than half a million years ago.

Based on the discovery of several remarkably well-preserved murals, the inhabitants appeared to be avian in biology. A rough transliteration of their language indicates they called themselves the Krazura.

descriptions.zh:
进一步的挖掘带来了一个惊人的发现：一个如此巨大的洞穴，足以容纳这个行星上较小的一些山脉。尽管它的建筑规模令人敬畏，但这个“大厅”却没有明显的功能，只有一个出入口。

这个大致呈球形的大厅内壁上遗留有强力的维度扭曲的证据；可以合理得出结论，这个密室是围绕虫洞或其他亚空间传送门的。

更重要的是，大殿外蚀刻的一幅壁画提供了一个令人难以置信的发现：这颗行星不是别的正是斯卡拉维德，是著名的舰队司令斯克兰德·夏普比克的祖先的居住地！
descriptions.en:
Further excavation has resulted in a startling discovery: a chamber so massive it could house one of the planet's smaller mountains. Despite the awesome scale of its construction, this 'Grand Hall' serves no apparent function, with only a single means of entrance and egress.

Roughly spherical, the chamber's walls show strong evidence of dimensional warping; it is reasonable to conclude that the chamber was built around a wormhole or some other subspace portal.

What's more, a mural etched just outside the Hall provided an incredible discovery: this planet is none other than Skravird, ancestral home of the famous Admiral Skrand Sharpbeak!

descriptions.zh:
进一步的挖掘带来了一个惊人的发现：一个如此巨大的洞穴，足以容纳这个行星上较小的一些山脉。尽管它的建筑规模令人敬畏，但这个“大厅”却没有明显的功能，只有一个出入口。

这个大致呈球形的大厅内壁上遗留有强力的维度扭曲的证据；可以合理得出结论，这个密室是围绕虫洞或其他亚空间传送门的。

这座大厅外蚀刻的壁画表明这颗行星曾经被称为斯卡拉维德。
descriptions.en:
Further excavation has resulted in a startling discovery: a chamber so massive it could house one of the planet's smaller mountains. Despite the awesome scale of its construction, this 'Grand Hall' serves no apparent function, with only a single means of entrance and egress.

Roughly spherical, the chamber's walls show strong evidence of dimensional warping; it is reasonable to conclude that the chamber was built around a wormhole or some other subspace portal.

A mural etched just outside the Hall indicates this planet was once called Skravird.

tooltips.zh: 这颗行星的名字被改为§Y斯卡拉维德§!

descriptions.zh:
你找到了斯卡拉维德。我本以为我永远地失去了家园。

有机会我会把我的爪子插入它的土里，感受着温暖的南风吹拂我的羽毛... 你为我和我的人民所做的一切都无法估量。

我的身体和心灵都感到焕然一新。我对你心怀感激。
descriptions.en:
You have found Skravird. I thought my home lost forever.

To have the chance to set my talons into its ground, to feel the warm south wind blowing through my feathers... What you have done for me and for my people is beyond measure.

I am refreshed, in body and mind. You have my gratitude.

descriptions.zh:
我们已经确定了这个克拉祖拉并非来自我们维度。他们通过某种类型的传送门抵达这里，发现自己漂流到一个陌生的外星星系中。很久以后，他们在到达的地点周围建造了这个大厅。

仅存的几份记录表明，他们认为自己是伟大而神秘力量的仲裁者。他们的最高领袖，被称为“亚库拉”，被认为是一种独立的个体，每一代都会转移到一个新的身体里。

在大厅下面，我们挖出了几位统治者的遗骸。有趣的是，最早的统治者与后面的统治者有着不同的基因结构。似乎是前往这个宇宙的旅程的影响了克拉祖拉的DNA，导致“复”眼的出现。
descriptions.en:
We have established that the Krazura were not native to our dimension. Arriving through a portal of some kind, they found themselves adrift in a strange and alien galaxy. Much later, the Grand Hall was built around their arrival site.

The few remaining records indicate they viewed themselves as arbiters of great and mystical power. Their supreme leader, known as the 'Yakura', was believed to be a single individual, reincarnating into a new body with each generation.

Beneath the Grand Hall, we unearthed the remains of several such rulers. Interestingly, the earliest possessed a different genetic structure from those that followed. It seems the journey to this universe impacted the Krazura's very DNA, resulting in the emergence of a 'double' set of eyes.

options.script: name = INTERESTING

options.conditions: exclusive_trigger = { owner = { has_origin = origin_evolutionary_predators } }

descriptions.zh:
克拉祖拉最初是我们宇宙中的难民。然而，在大殿附近发现的记录表明，他们迅速建立起了一个强大的星际帝国。他们的人民在多个世代的时间里保持着繁荣昌盛。亚库拉的能力和至高无上的地位毋庸置疑。然后，“威胁”出现了。

这个无名的敌人和他们以前遇到的敌人都不一样，似乎一心要毁灭他们。亚库拉这个最伟大的圣贤们在这强大的威胁面前无能为力，他们强大的才能变得毫无用处。
descriptions.en:
The Krazura started out as refugees in our universe. Nevertheless, records discovered near the Grand Hall show that they quickly established themselves as a powerful interstellar empire. For many generations they enjoyed a Golden Age. Their people prospered, and the ability and supremacy of the Yakura went unquestioned. Then the Menace appeared.

A foe unlike any they had encountered before, this nameless enemy seemed obsessed with their destruction. The Krazura's greatest sages stood powerless before the indomitable threat, their mighty magic rendered useless.

descriptions.zh:
我们发现了一批记录，为了解克拉祖拉的命运提供了线索。

指挥他们海军旗舰的是一位传奇的舰队司令，他是他人民的伟大英雄。在被外星威胁取得最后的胜利之前，他和他的船员们被派遣执行了最后且大胆的任务。为了绕过敌人，他们进入了一个未经测试的星门。自此，这艘船和它的船员们便再也没有了任何音讯。

这中间发生了什么仍然是一个谜。这艘舰船是否仍有存在可能？
descriptions.en:
We have uncovered a cache of records that offer clues as to the fate of the Krazura.

Commanding their navy's flagship was a legendary Admiral, a great hero of his people. Before the alien Menace could achieve a final victory, he and his crew were sent on a last, daring mission. In a bid to outflank the enemy, they entered an untested Gateway. The ship and its crew were never heard from again.

What happened remains a mystery. Is it possible that this ship is still out there?

descriptions.zh:
我们发现了一批记录，为了解克拉祖拉的命运提供了线索。

为了大胆地绕过敌人，亚库拉命令旗舰穿过未经测试的星门。舰队司令正是传奇的斯克兰德·夏普比克。

他和他的船员们继承了一项非凡的遗产。无论斯克兰德是否愿意接受这个头衔，他的人民现在将他视为亚库拉。
descriptions.en:
We have uncovered a cache of records that offer clues as to the fate of the Krazura.

In a daring bid to outflank the enemy, the Yakura ordered the flagship to enter an untested Gateway. In command was the legendary Admiral Skrand Sharpbeak.

He and his crew are the inheritors of a remarkable legacy. Whether Skrand wishes to accept the title or not, his people now look to him as Yakura.

descriptions.zh:
尽管整体进度迟滞不前，我们的[owner.GetResearchers]还是发现了一个以前未被发现的房间。在里面，有一座庞大的雕像，壮观又美丽。

形态是鸟类，长而有力的脖子由金属链条构成，不知为何能够悬浮在上面。锐利的羽毛从仪态端庄的颅骨上迸发出来，它黄金般的眼睛象征着权利。在穿过大厅时，[owner.GetResearchers]有一种不舒服的感觉，仿佛在被人窥视。

他们在这个雕像后面发现了一个隐藏的门或封印，不管这只不祥之鸟是在守卫什么，它的守护物早已失效。
descriptions.en:
Even as overall progress stalled, our [owner.GetResearchers] revealed the entrance to a previously undiscovered chamber. Inside was a massive statue, as imposing as it is beautiful.

Avian in form, its long, powerful neck is fashioned of metallic links that somehow manage to hover in place. Sharp plumage erupts from a patrician skull, and its eyes are golden heralds of power. Moving through the chamber, our [owner.GetResearchers] had the uncomfortable sensation that they were being watched.

Behind the figure they discovered hidden a door or seal, but whatever this baleful bird was guarding has long since ceased to function.

options.script: name = INTERESTING

descriptions.zh:
根据我们迄今为止的发现，这个文明对于悲剧并不陌生。

储存在某种地下墓室或陵墓里的古老记录详细描述了一场大规模瘟疫的爆发，这场瘟疫以一种特别可怕的方式影响着这个鸟类物种的生理特征。

最初，表现为羽毛上的问题，病毒导致羽毛从根部开始腐烂。在几天内，这些病症就会扩散到了血液中。尽管我们无法确定，但初步估计将死亡率超过30%。

一座令人心酸的纪念碑竖立在了城市中心的一个广场上。在一堆骨头上，一只骷髅鸟绝望地看着天空，它掉落的羽毛散落在一对脆弱的爪子上。
descriptions.en:
Based on what we have discovered thus far, this civilization was no stranger to tragedy.

Ancient records stored in some kind of crypt or mausoleum detail the emergence of a great plague, one which afflicted the species' avian physiognomy in particularly gruesome ways.

First manifesting in the plumage, the virus caused feathers to rot at the root. Within days, these effects had spread to the blood. We cannot know for certain, but early estimates place the mortality rate at over 30%.

A poignant monument was erected in one of the city's central squares. Atop a mound of bones, a single, skeletal bird looks hopelessly to the sky, its fallen feathers strewn about a pair of brittle talons.
